# Visual System

Translate the selected direction into an executable visual language.

Before implementation, present this system using the [visual proposal requirements](visual-proposal.md). Inspect the client's CIS pages and canonical motifs when available. If CIS is partial or absent, follow that reference's proposal and discussion process: distinguish official assets, inferred conventions and proposed additions; obtain agreement on missing design decisions. Visual approval does not approve motion; follow [motion proposal requirements](motion-proposal.md) separately.

## Color System

Define colors by function, not only HEX values: background, primary, accent, energy, interface, CTA, status, warning, atmospheric tone.

## Lighting System

Define intended sources and roles: environment light, brand light, interactive light, product/character light, effect light, transition light.

## Material System

Define the material vocabulary appropriate to the brand: glass, metal, fabric, organic, stone, liquid, crystal, fog, dust, energy, paper, plastic, etc. Do not include materials merely because they are fashionable.

## Typography System

Define roles such as:
- Display type for world/brand/emotion,
- Interface/body type for reading, navigation, data, price, and conversion.

Specify hierarchy, line-breaking attitude, density, and motion behavior.

## UI Language

Define navigation, buttons, cards, tags/status, numbering, dividers, icons, hover/touch feedback, progress, loading, and CTA behavior.

## Image / Asset Direction

Classify assets:
1. canonical client assets,
2. generated/supporting assets,
3. technical effect assets,
4. 3D assets,
5. 2.5D layered assets.

Define crop, masking, layering, depth, and compositing rules.

## Shader / Particle Language

Define behavior, not just appearance. Example states:
Idle -> Hover/Proximity -> Activation -> Transition -> Release.

## 2.5D Strategy

When full 3D is unnecessary or unavailable, use source images with layer separation, depth maps, parallax, camera motion, fog, particles, lighting, masks, and shaders to create spatial depth while preserving original art.
